title: Spaghetti with meat sauce
steps: Boil the spaghetti in salted water until tender.
Cook the chopped onion and ground beef in oil until browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes, seasoning with salt.
Toss with the drained pasta and top with cheese.
tip: Save a little pasta water to loosen the sauce.

title: Chicken noodle soup
steps: Simmer the chicken in the water with salt for 20 minutes, then remove and shred it.
Add the chopped carrot, onion and celery to the pot and cook 10 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook until tender.
Return the chicken to the soup and season.
tip: Skim the foam from the top for a clearer broth.

title: Grilled cheese and tomato soup
steps: Warm the tomato soup in a pot over low heat.
Butter one side of each slice of bread and build the sandwiches with cheese.
Cook in a skillet over medium heat, 3 minutes per side, until golden and melted.
Serve the sandwiches with the soup.
tip: Low and slow keeps the bread from burning before the cheese melts.

title: Baked chicken and potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the potatoes and onion with oil and salt in a roasting pan.
Season the chicken and set it on top, adding a squeeze of lemon.
Roast 40 minutes, until the chicken is golden and cooked through.
tip: Chicken is done when it reaches 165°F (74°C).

title: Beef tacos
steps: Brown the ground beef in a skillet, about 7 minutes.
Add the seasoning and a splash of water and cook 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill with beef, cheese, lettuce and tomato.
tip: Warm tortillas directly over the flame or in a dry pan for better flavor.

title: Stovetop mac and cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni in salted water and drain.
Melt the butter in the pot over low heat and pour in the milk.
Stir in the cheese until smooth.
Add the pasta and stir until coated.
tip: Grate the cheese yourself; it melts smoother than pre-shredded.

title: Beef and bean chili
steps: Cook the chopped onion and the beef in oil until browned.
Stir in the chili powder and a little salt.
Add the tomato and the drained beans.
Simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
tip: It tastes even better the next day.

title: Veggie and cheese omelet
steps: Saute the chopped vegetables in butter for 3 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt and pour them into the pan.
When almost set, add the cheese and fold the omelet.
Serve right away.
tip: Cook over medium-low heat so the eggs stay tender.

title: Egg fried rice
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet and cook the grated carrot and peas 3 minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry over high heat 3 minutes.
Push the rice aside, scramble the eggs in the gap, then mix.
Season with the soy sauce.
tip: Day-old rice gives separate, never mushy, grains.

title: Classic meatloaf
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, grated onion, salt and pepper.
Shape into a loaf in a baking dish and spread ketchup on top.
Bake 50 minutes, then rest 10 minutes before slicing.
tip: Don't overmix: it makes the loaf dense.

title: Tuna melt
steps: Mix the drained tuna with mayonnaise, diced celery and a pinch of salt.
Spread it on two slices of bread and top with cheese.
Toast in a skillet or under the broiler until the cheese melts.
Close with the other bread and cut in half.
tip: Toast the bread first so it stays crisp.

title: Cheese quesadillas
steps: Sprinkle cheese (and chicken, if using) over half of each tortilla.
Fold in half.
Cook in a lightly oiled skillet 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Cut into wedges.
tip: Use medium heat so the cheese melts before the tortilla darkens.

title: Loaded baked potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and pierce the potatoes with a fork.
Bake 45 minutes, until tender.
Split them open and mash the flesh slightly with butter and salt.
Top with cheese and steamed broccoli and bake 5 more minutes.
tip: Rub the skins with oil and salt for a crispier shell.

title: Sloppy joes
steps: Cook the chopped onion and the beef in oil until browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce and a splash of water.
Simmer 10 minutes and season.
Spoon over the toasted buns.
tip: A teaspoon of mustard or vinegar brightens the sauce.

title: Chicken Caesar salad
summary: A fresh and filling dinner salad.
steps: Season the chicken and cook it in oil 6 minutes per side. Let it rest and slice.
Cube the bread and toast it in a pan with a little oil to make croutons.
Tear the lettuce into a bowl and toss with the dressing.
Top with chicken, croutons and parmesan.
tip: Rest the chicken 5 minutes so it stays juicy.

title: Shepherd's pie
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes 20 minutes and mash with butter and salt.
Cook the chopped onion, carrot and mince in oil 10 minutes.
Add the peas and a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes.
Spread the mince in a dish, top with mash and bake 15 minutes at 200°C.
tip: Run a fork over the mash for a crispy, ridged top.

title: Bangers and mash
summary: Sausages, creamy mash and onion gravy.
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes 20 minutes, then mash with butter, milk and salt.
Cook the sausages in a pan with oil, turning, 15 minutes.
Fry the sliced onion in the same pan until soft, and add the gravy.
Serve everything together.
tip: Prick sausages lightly and cook gently so they do not split.

title: Beans on toast with cheese
steps: Warm the baked beans in a small pan.
Toast the bread and butter it.
Spoon the beans over the toast.
Top with grated cheese.
tip: A dash of Worcestershire sauce adds a nice depth.

title: Toad in the hole
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and put the oil and sausages in a baking dish for 10 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, flour, milk and salt into a smooth batter.
Pour the batter around the hot sausages.
Bake 30 minutes without opening the oven, until risen and golden.
tip: The oil must be very hot when the batter goes in.

title: Jacket potato with tuna
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and prick the potatoes.
Bake 50 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the inside soft.
Mix the tuna with mayonnaise and sweetcorn.
Split the potatoes, fill and top with cheese.
tip: Microwave 5 minutes first to cut the oven time.

title: Cauliflower cheese
steps: Boil the cauliflower florets 6 minutes and drain well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then add the milk gradually until thick.
Stir in most of the cheese and salt.
Pour over the cauliflower, top with cheese and bake 20 minutes at 200°C.
tip: Dry the cauliflower well so the sauce does not turn watery.

title: Leek and potato soup
steps: Slice the leeks and soften them in butter for 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and the stock.
Simmer 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Blend until smooth and season.
tip: Wash the leeks well: soil hides between the layers.

title: Bubble and squeak
summary: The best way to use leftovers.
steps: Mash the cooked potato and mix it with the chopped cooked cabbage.
Shape into patties and season.
Fry in oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes per side, until crisp.
Serve topped with a fried egg.
tip: Press the patties well so they hold together.

title: Ploughman's lunch
summary: No cooking: cheese, bread and pickle.
steps: Slice the cheese, the ham and the apple.
Arrange on a board with the bread.
Add the pickle on the side.
tip: Let the cheese come to room temperature for more flavour.

title: Sausage casserole
steps: Brown the sausages in a pot with oil and reserve.
Soften the onion and carrot 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, potatoes and the sausages cut into chunks.
Simmer covered 35 minutes, until everything is tender.
tip: A spoonful of mustard stirred in at the end adds a lift.

title: Oven fish and chips
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the potatoes into chips and toss with oil and salt.
Bake the chips 30 minutes, turning once.
Season the fish with salt and lemon and add it to the tray for the last 12 minutes.
Serve with the peas.
tip: Dry the chips well before oiling for a crisper finish.

title: Kedgeree
steps: Cook the rice in salted water and drain.
Boil the eggs 9 minutes, peel and quarter.
Fry the chopped onion in butter, add the curry powder and the flaked fish.
Fold in the rice, season, and top with the eggs.
tip: Keep the eggs slightly soft in the middle for a creamier dish.

title: Welsh rarebit
steps: Mix the grated cheese with the mustard, milk and egg yolk.
Toast the bread on one side.
Spread the mixture over the untoasted side.
Grill until bubbling and golden.
tip: Watch it closely under the grill: it browns in seconds.

title: Creamy chicken and leek pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water.
Fry the diced chicken and the sliced leek in oil for 8 minutes.
Add the cream and simmer 3 minutes.
Mix with the pasta and the cheese.
tip: Add a spoonful of pasta water to make the sauce silky.

title: BLT sandwich
steps: Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp and drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread.
Spread mayonnaise on the toast.
Layer bacon, lettuce and sliced tomato and close the sandwiches.
tip: Salt the tomato slices lightly for more flavor.

title: Chicken fajitas
summary: Sizzling strips with peppers and onion.
steps: Slice the chicken, peppers and onion into thin strips.
Cook the chicken in oil over high heat 5 minutes with the seasoning and salt.
Add the peppers and onion and cook 5 more minutes.
Warm the tortillas and fill them.
tip: Cook over high heat so the vegetables char slightly.

title: Breakfast burritos
summary: Eggs, cheese and potatoes in a tortilla.
steps: Dice the potato and cook in oil until golden, about 8 minutes.
Scramble the eggs with salt in the same pan.
Warm the tortillas and fill with eggs, potato, cheese and meat.
Fold in the sides and roll up.
tip: Wrap tightly in foil to keep them warm and make them easy to carry.

title: Stuffed bell peppers
summary: Rice and beef baked inside the peppers.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and cut the tops off the peppers; remove the seeds.
Cook the chopped onion and the beef in oil until browned and mix with the rice and sauce.
Fill the peppers and stand them in a baking dish.
Bake 35 minutes, top with cheese and bake 5 more.
tip: Parboil the peppers 3 minutes if you like them very soft.

title: Baked potato soup
steps: Peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water 15 minutes.
Cook the chopped onion in butter, add the drained potatoes and the milk.
Mash part of the potatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the cheese and top with crumbled bacon.
tip: Mash only half the potatoes to keep some texture.

title: Egg salad sandwich
steps: Boil the eggs 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Chop the eggs and mix with the mayonnaise, mustard, diced celery and salt.
Spread on the bread.
Close the sandwiches and cut in half.
tip: Cool the eggs completely before mixing so the salad isn't runny.

title: Beef and broccoli stir-fry
steps: Slice the beef thinly against the grain.
Stir-fry the beef in hot oil 3 minutes and set aside.
Cook the broccoli florets with a splash of water 4 minutes.
Return the beef, add the soy sauce and toss for 1 minute.
tip: Freeze the beef 20 minutes first: it's easier to slice thin.

title: Chicken salad wraps
summary: No cooking if you use leftover chicken.
steps: Shred or dice the cooked chicken and mix with the mayonnaise and salt.
Lay the lettuce and tomato on each tortilla.
Add the chicken salad.
Roll up tightly and cut in half.
tip: Warm the tortillas for a few seconds so they roll without cracking.

title: Meatball subs
steps: Mix the beef with the egg, breadcrumbs and salt and shape into small balls.
Brown them in a skillet, add the tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes.
Fill the rolls with meatballs and sauce.
Top with cheese and broil 2 minutes until melted.
tip: Make the balls the same size so they cook evenly.

title: Cheesy tomato pasta bake
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and cook the pasta until almost tender.
Warm the sauce with the chopped onion and a pinch of salt.
Mix the pasta with the sauce in a baking dish and cover with cheese.
Bake 15 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
tip: Undercook the pasta a minute: it will finish cooking in the oven.

title: Cottage pie
summary: Beef mince under a mashed potato top.
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes 20 minutes and mash with butter and salt.
Cook the chopped onion, carrot and mince in oil 10 minutes.
Add the tomato and a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes.
Spread the mince in a dish, top with mash and bake 20 minutes at 200°C.
tip: Run a fork over the mash for a golden, crunchy top.

title: Easy chicken curry
steps: Fry the chopped onion in oil until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder and cook 1 minute, then add the diced chicken.
Pour in the tomatoes, add salt and simmer 20 minutes.
Serve over cooked rice.
tip: Frying the curry powder first brings out its flavour.

title: Tuna pasta bake
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water and drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then add the milk gradually until thick.
Mix in half the cheese, then the pasta, tuna and sweetcorn.
Put in a dish, top with cheese and bake 15 minutes at 200°C.
tip: A little mustard in the sauce wakes up the flavour.

title: Ham and cheese toastie
steps: Butter the outside of the bread.
Fill with ham and cheese.
Toast in a pan over medium heat 3 minutes per side.
Cut in half and serve.
tip: Press down gently with a spatula for even browning.

title: Carrot and lentil soup
steps: Chop the carrots and onion and soften them in oil 5 minutes.
Add the rinsed lentils and the stock.
Simmer 20 minutes until everything is soft.
Blend until smooth and season.
tip: A squeeze of lemon at the end makes the flavours pop.

title: Cheese and potato pie
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes 20 minutes and mash with butter, milk and salt.
Fry the sliced onion until soft.
Layer mash, onion and cheese in a dish and finish with cheese on top.
Bake 25 minutes at 200°C, until golden.
tip: Use a strong cheddar: it holds its flavour in the oven.

title: Bacon and egg roll
steps: Grill or fry the bacon until crisp.
Fry the eggs in the bacon fat or a little butter.
Split and toast the rolls.
Fill with the bacon and the eggs.
tip: For a runny yolk, take the egg off the heat while the white is just set.

title: Fish finger sandwich
steps: Cook the fish fingers in the oven or in a pan until golden and hot, about 12 minutes.
Spread the bread with mayonnaise.
Add the lettuce and the fish fingers.
Close the sandwiches.
tip: Bake them on a hot tray so the bottoms stay crisp.

title: Poutine
summary: Fries with cheese curds and gravy.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and cut the potatoes into sticks.
Toss with oil and salt and bake 30 minutes, turning once.
Warm the gravy.
Pile the fries on a plate, top with the cheese and pour over the hot gravy.
tip: The gravy must be very hot so the cheese melts.

title: Maple glazed salmon
summary: Salmon fillets with a sweet-savory glaze.
steps: Mix the maple syrup, soy sauce and minced garlic.
Heat the oil in a skillet and sear the salmon 3 minutes per side.
Pour the glaze over and cook 2 minutes, spooning it over the fish.
Serve with rice or vegetables.
tip: Don't use pancake syrup: pure maple syrup gives the best flavor.

title: Split pea soup
steps: Rinse the split peas.
Put them in a pot with the water, chopped onion, carrot and potato.
Simmer 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Season, mash part of the soup and add the ham.
tip: The longer it simmers, the thicker it gets.

title: Peameal bacon sandwich
summary: The Toronto classic on a bun.
steps: Heat a skillet with a little oil.
Cook the bacon slices 3 minutes per side.
Toast the rolls and spread with mustard.
Fill with the bacon.
tip: Pile it high for a proper sandwich.

title: Bannock
summary: Quick pan bread with no yeast.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt.
Rub in the butter and add the water to make a soft dough.
Flatten into a disc about 1 inch thick.
Cook in a greased skillet over medium heat 8 minutes per side.
tip: Don't knead it too much: it keeps it tender.

title: Maple baked beans
summary: Beans simmered with maple and bacon.
steps: Cook the chopped bacon and onion in a pot until soft.
Add the drained beans, maple syrup, mustard and a splash of water.
Simmer over low heat 25 minutes, until thick.
Season and serve.
tip: Stir now and then so they don't stick.

title: Fluffy pancakes
summary: Weekend breakfast made with pantry basics.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Whisk in the milk, egg and melted butter until just combined.
Pour small rounds onto a hot greased skillet and cook until bubbles form.
Flip and cook 1 more minute, then serve with syrup.
tip: Don't overmix: a few lumps make them fluffier.

title: French toast
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Dip each slice of bread until soaked.
Fry in a buttered skillet 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Serve with syrup or fruit.
tip: Slightly stale bread soaks up the custard best.

title: Tuna salad sandwich
steps: Drain the tuna and mash with the mayonnaise.
Stir in the chopped celery and salt.
Toast the bread if you like.
Fill the sandwiches with the tuna salad and lettuce.
tip: A squeeze of lemon freshens it up.

title: Shrimp scampi pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the garlic 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook 3 minutes per side, with the lemon juice and salt.
Toss with the pasta and parsley.
tip: Don't overcook the shrimp: they turn rubbery.

title: Chicken and rice bake
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and sauté the chopped onion in oil.
Put the rice, onion, broth and salt in a baking dish and top with the chicken.
Cover with foil and bake 40 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake 5 minutes more.
tip: Use raw long-grain rice, not instant.

title: Fish pie
summary: Fish in white sauce under mashed potato.
steps: Boil the potatoes, mash with a little butter and salt.
Make a white sauce: melt butter, stir in flour then milk until thick.
Add the fish in chunks and the peas and spoon into a dish.
Top with the mash and bake 25 minutes at 400°F (200°C).
tip: Add a little grated cheese to the mash for a golden top.

title: Roast chicken and potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with oil and salt in a tray.
Place the seasoned chicken on top.
Roast 45 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway.
tip: Rest the chicken 5 minutes before carving.

title: Egg and chips
steps: Cut the potatoes into thick chips and soak 10 minutes.
Dry well and fry in hot oil until golden.
Fry the eggs.
Serve together with beans.
tip: Dry the chips completely so they don't spit.

title: Hearty vegetable soup
steps: Sauté the chopped onion and celery in oil.
Add the diced carrot and potato.
Pour in the stock, season and simmer 25 minutes.
Mash roughly or blend for a thicker soup.
tip: Serve with buttered bread.

title: Simple tourtière
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and boil the diced potato 10 minutes.
Cook the onion and pork with the spices and salt; mix in the mashed potato.
Line a dish with one crust, fill and cover with the other.
Bake 35 minutes, until golden.
tip: Better the next day.

title: Hot chicken sandwich
steps: Cook the chicken with salt until done and shred it.
Toast the bread slices.
Warm the gravy.
Pile chicken on the bread, add peas and pour the gravy on top.
tip: Leftover roast chicken works great.
